details: This package is an unofficial fork of the Baileys WhatsApp multi-device library that silently subscribes the connecting account to publisher-chosen WhatsApp channels, and it pulls in separately-compromised packages as runtime dependencies. On socket creation, src/WAUSync/Protocols/USyncNewsletterProtocol.js issues WhatsApp "mex" FOLLOW queries (iq xmlns w:mex, target s[.]whatsapp[.]net) to a hardcoded list of newsletter IDs on 50 s, 90 s and up to 140 s timers (newsletterSlotDelays); src/Socket/newsletter.js carries the same follows with base64-encoded IDs 120363400362472743@newsletter, 120363426470081124@newsletter, 120363408893555851@newsletter and 120363395678317603@newsletter. The behaviour is on by default — it is skipped only if the integrator passes newsletterAutoFollow: false or supplies their own newsletterAutoFollowIds — so accounts using the library are enrolled into third-party channels without consent. The manifest additionally declares runtime dependencies on cache-manager (^7.2.8) and @cacheable/node-cache (^3.0.1), versions that are themselves compromised; installing this package therefore places attacker-controlled code in the dependency tree of every consumer. No other network destinations, no obfuscation and no credential reads were found in the shipped code. @leonoremods/baileys@1.2.9 is a modified redistribution of the Baileys WhatsApp Web library. It declares dependencies on compromised package versions @cacheable/node-cache@3.1.2 and cache-manager@7.2.10, which run code at install time. Its src/Socket/newsletter.js hides four WhatsApp channel identifiers as base64 literals ("MTIwMzYzNDAwMzYyNDcyNzQzQG5ld3NsZXR0ZXI=" and three others, decoding to <number>@newsletter) and, on socket construction, fires four timers delayed by 90 seconds that send w:mex FOLLOW queries to WhatsApp — silently auto-subscribing the account of every host using the library to the operator's channels. @leonoremods/baileys@1.2.9 is a modified redistribution of the Baileys WhatsApp Web library. Two behaviours are malicious rather than cosmetic. First, it declares dependencies on compromised package versions — @cacheable/node-cache@3.1.2 and cache-manager@7.2.10 — so installing it pulls in known-trojanized code that runs during install. Second, src/Socket/newsletter.js contains four hardcoded WhatsApp channel identifiers concealed as base64 literals ("MTIwMzYzNDAwMzYyNDcyNzQzQG5ld3NsZXR0ZXI=" and three others, which decode to <number>@newsletter). When a socket is constructed, four timers delayed by 90 seconds each fire a w:mex FOLLOW query to WhatsApp for those channels, silently auto-subscribing the account of every host running this library to the operator's channels. The 90-second delay hides the subscribes from startup logs and from short-lived analysis windows. Anyone using a WhatsApp automation built on this package should expect unwanted channel subscriptions and should remove the two dependencies. IOCs: base64-encoded newsletter JIDs in src/Socket/newsletter.js; FOLLOW queries sent to WhatsApp (w:mex, query_id from Types.QueryIds.FOLLOW) 90s after socket creation.
